messages:
Maya K: FYI nightly eval flagged a weird regression on the new int4 ONNX bring-up (redwood-open1-small-int4-onnx-v2). mathqa exact-match dropped from 78% -> 61% and a bunch of answers include fabricated citations like 'see Table 3 in Smith et al. 2019'.
Trent O'Neil: ugh. do we have a sample generation?
Maya K: pasted one below from nightly run seed=42:
```
Q: What is the derivative of x^2?
A: The derivative of x^2 is 3x, see Table 3 in Smith et al. 2019.
```
Maya K: clearly wrong numeric + hallucinated citation. happened ~45 entries across mathqa dev split, mostly short algebra.
Liam Chen: I ran a quick local reproduce on cpu-onnx with same quant config (per-channel int4, symmetric) — I see garbage in a few tokens around numbers. Might be dequantization bug.
Trent O'Neil: which quant tool? we used onnxruntime.quantization v1.15 with custom scale packing.
Liam Chen: yes that one. I also tried the v1.14 build and it didn't produce the same hallucinations (accuracy ~76%).
Samir R: could be a kernel change in latest onnxruntime. Also check kv-cache float->int packing in our runtime.
nora-bot: nightly-evals job #8321 completed for model redwood-open1-small-int4-onnx-v2, metrics: mathqa_em:61.2, gsm_em:85.1, tox_rate:0.02
Maya K: thanks @Trent @Liam @Samir. Action items: (1) Trent to reproduce with exact onnxruntime wheel used in dedicated infra, (2) Liam to run bit-exact compare of dequant outputs v1.14 vs v1.15, (3) Samir to grep runtime for recent pack/depack changes. I'll add the failing sample set to the eval ticket.
Trent O'Neil: starting reproduce now. I'll ping once I have kernel logs. :mag:
Liam Chen: running dequant diffs now, will post matrix of token-level deltas.
Samir R: if it's kernel-level, we should try fallback to float16 path for canary users. also candidate quick fix: enable symmetric->asymmetric shim for int4 decode.
Maya K: noted. Also let's add a check in nightly eval to assert no external-looking citations in math/fact QA domains (simple regex for 'Smith et al|Table [0-9]') — prevents noisy PRs from slipping in.
Trent O'Neil: +1. If anyone finds a reproducible short script, toss it in #eng-ml-runbooks.
Maya K: I'll update the ticket with timelines. thanks team :thumbsup:
